questions.title: Factorial by Recursion
questions.description:
The classic first recursion: n! grows fast, so the answer is a long. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long factorial(int n)

It must return n! with 0! = 1 and 1! = 1. Implement it recursively: a base case, then n * factorial(n - 1).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with n!.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 20

questions.title: Fibonacci Term
questions.description:
The Fibonacci sequence starts fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1, and every later term is the sum of the two before it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long fibTerm(int n)

It must return fib(n). A plain recursive solution is fast enough for these limits.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with fib(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Digit Sum by Recursion
questions.description:
Peel digits off with % 10 and / 10 until the base case 0 is reached. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long digitSum(long n)

It must return the sum of the decimal digits of n (digitSum(0) = 0).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the digit sum.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: GCD by Euclid
questions.description:
Euclid's algorithm is recursion at its cleanest: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) until b hits 0. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long gcd(long a, long b)

It must return the greatest common divisor of a and b (both at least 1).

Input Format:
Line 1: a. Line 2: b.

Output Format:
One line with gcd(a, b).

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: Reverse a Word by Recursion
questions.description:
Build the mirror of a word one character at a time: reverse everything after the first character, then append that character at the end. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String reverseWord(String s)

It must return s reversed. A recursive solution is expected (substring plus first character works at these sizes).

Input Format:
One line with the word s (lowercase letters, no spaces).

Output Format:
One line with s reversed.

Constraints:
1 <= length(s) <= 300

questions.title: Sum One To N by Recursion
questions.description:
The simplest call-stack drill: sum(n) = n + sum(n - 1) down to sum(1) = 1. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long sumToN(int n)

It must return 1 + 2 + ... + n. Implement it recursively.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Ways
questions.description:
A stairmaster counts the ways to reach step n when each move climbs 1 or 2 steps — the count follows the Fibonacci recurrence. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long climbWays(int n)

ways(0) = 1, ways(1) = 1 and ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). It must return the number of distinct move sequences.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Palindrome Check by Recursion
questions.description:
A spell checker validates words by comparing the outer letters and recursing inward until the pointers cross — the base case does the work. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isPalindrome(String s)

It must return 1 when s reads the same forwards and backwards, else 0. Implement the inward comparison recursively.

Input Format:
One line with the word s (lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= length(s) <= 200

questions.title: Triangular Cup Stack
questions.description:
A cafe stacks cups in a triangle: row k holds k cups, so a full stack of n rows holds T(n) = n + T(n-1) cups with T(0) = 0. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long triangleCount(int n)

It must return T(n) computed recursively.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with T(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 5000

questions.title: Countdown Echo
questions.description:
A launch console echoes the countdown recursively: print n, then echo the rest. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String countdownEcho(int n)

It must return the numbers n, n-1, ..., 1 joined by single spaces, where echo(1) = "1" and echo(n) = n + " " + echo(n-1).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the countdown.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500

questions.title: Fast Power Modulo
questions.description:
Encryption needs b^e mod m where e can be astronomical — binary exponentiation halves the exponent at every recursive call and squares the base. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long fastPower(long b, long e, long m)

It must return (b^e) mod m, with b^0 = 1. Implement it recursively WITHOUT loops — the recursion tree halves the exponent: fastPower(b, e, m) squares fastPower(b, e/2, m) and multiplies by b once more when e is odd, reducing mod m at every step.

Input Format:
Line 1: b. Line 2: e. Line 3: m.

Output Format:
One line with (b^e) mod m.

Constraints:
0 <= b <= 1000000000, 0 <= e <= 1000000000000000000, 1 <= m <= 2000000000

questions.title: Count Subsets With Sum S
questions.description:
A gift box can pack any subset of n items; the packer counts how many subsets weigh exactly S grams. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long subsetSumCount(int[] arr, int s)

Each item is used at most once; the empty subset counts when s = 0. It must return the number of subsets summing to s — recurse include/exclude over the items.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: s.

Output Format:
One line with the subset count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000, 0 <= s <= 20000

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Moves
questions.description:
Moving n disks between pegs takes a famously precise number of single-disk moves: move n-1 disks aside, step the biggest disk over, move n-1 disks back. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long hanoiMoves(int n)

moves(1) = 1 and moves(n) = 2 * moves(n-1) + 1. It must return the number of moves for n disks (use long — n reaches 40).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the move count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Distinct Permutations of a Word
questions.description:
A badge printer lists every DISTINCT arrangement of a word's letters; repeated letters collapse duplicates, so the count is len! divided by the factorials of the letter multiplicities. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long permutationCount(String s)

It must return the number of distinct permutations of the characters of s.

Input Format:
One line with the word s (lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct arrangements.

Constraints:
1 <= length(s) <= 20

questions.title: Josephus Survivor
questions.description:
The elimination circle: n people numbered 1..n, counting starts at person 1 and every k-th person leaves; counting resumes around the circle until one survivor remains. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int josephusSurvivor(int n, int k)

The recursive rank formula: survivor(1) = 1 and survivor(n) = ((survivor(n-1) + k - 1) mod n) + 1. It must return the survivor's number.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: k.

Output Format:
One line with the survivor's number.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 500

questions.title: Next Permutation
questions.description:
A word generator produces the NEXT lexicographic arrangement: find the suffix that is already maximal, swap the pivot with the smallest larger letter on its right, then reverse the suffix. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String nextPermutation(String s)

It must return the next lexicographic permutation of s's characters; when s is already the highest permutation, return the lowest one (its characters sorted ascending).

Input Format:
One line with the word s (lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with the next permutation.

Constraints:
1 <= length(s) <= 8

questions.title: Nth Lexicographic Permutation
questions.description:
A combination lock lists all permutations of its distinct symbols in lexicographic order and must jump straight to the k-th one — factorial blocks decide each position: with r symbols remaining, every leading symbol owns (r-1)! complete blocks. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String kthPermutation(String s, int k)

s has distinct lowercase letters; k is 1-based and never exceeds the number of permutations. It must return the k-th permutation in lexicographic order.

Input Format:
Line 1: the string s (distinct lowercase letters). Line 2: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th permutation.

Constraints:
1 <= length(s) <= 8, 1 <= k <= length(s)!

questions.title: Count Subsets With Sum S Large
questions.description:
The gift packer is back with a bulk order: n up to 30 items with huge weights — brute force over 2^30 subsets is too slow. Split the array into two halves, enumerate every subset sum of each half, sort one half's sums, and for each sum of the other half binary-search how many complements hit S (meet in the middle). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long subsetSumCountBig(int[] arr, long s)

It must return the number of subsets (each index used at most once, empty subset sums to 0) with sum exactly s.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: s.

Output Format:
One line with the subset count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30, 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000, 0 <= s <= 30000000000

questions.title: N-Queens Solution Count
questions.description:
The classic backtracking drill: place n queens on an n x n board so none attack another — put one queen per row and recurse over columns, undoing placements that collide vertically or diagonally. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int nQueensCount(int n)

It must return the number of distinct solutions.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the solution count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8

questions.title: Balanced Parentheses in Order
questions.description:
A syntax generator lists every balanced sequence of n bracket pairs in lexicographic order ('(' sorts before ')'): at each position try '(' while any unused pair remains, then ')' while it closes an open bracket — this backtracking order is already lexicographic. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String balancedSet(int n)

It must return all 2n-character sequences in lexicographic order, separated by newline characters (no trailing newline needed).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
The valid sequences, one per line, in lexicographic order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 7
